title: TemplateSection.removeTemplate clears customer lookup with `dcfg_customer_id: null` — wrong payload shape
detail: Line 2104: `await apiPatch(`/${EntitySets.docTemplates}(${tplId})`, { dcfg_customer_id: null });` — this will not clear the customer lookup. To null a Dataverse lookup via Power Pages you must either PATCH with `{ 'dcfg_customer_id@odata.bind': null }` (same bind-name form the code uses to set it on line 2091) or DELETE the `/entity(id)/dcfg_customer_id/$ref`. Sending `dcfg_customer_id: null` as a plain property either throws 400 or is silently ignored. TemplateDetail.jsx line 641 uses the correct `'dcfg_customer_id@odata.bind': null` form. Net effect on the Admin → Customer Config → Custom Templates tab: 'Remove' button appears to succeed but the template stays linked to the customer.
evidence: Admin.jsx:2100-2108 removeTemplate function; compare to TemplateDetail.jsx:641 which uses the correct null-bind form.
recommendedFix: Change line 2104 to `await apiPatch(`/${EntitySets.docTemplates}(${tplId})`, { 'dcfg_customer_id@odata.bind': null });`. Same pattern as TemplateDetail.jsx:641.

title: TRADE_OPTIONS constant declared inside CostCodeForm — re-created on every render
detail: Line 891: `const TRADE_OPTIONS = [ ... ];` is declared inside the CostCodeForm component body, so a new array and 13 new option-objects are allocated every time the form re-renders. Not a performance hot path (form is short-lived) but the pattern is inconsistent with the module-level SECTIONS/NAV_ROUTES constants at the top of the file. Low priority.
evidence: Admin.jsx:891-905 — TRADE_OPTIONS inside function CostCodeForm.
recommendedFix: Hoist TRADE_OPTIONS out of CostCodeForm to module scope (near the other top-of-file constants).

title: DocumentTemplatesTab load + save errors only console.error — no user feedback
detail: Line 206 `catch (e) { console.error('Load templates:', e); }` and line 229 `catch (e) { console.error('Save template:', e); }` — same pattern repeats for OnboardingStepsTab (424, 447), LocationTypesTab (667, 688), CostCodesTab (802, 823), ApplianceTypesTab (977, 998), VendorsTab (1136, 1157), and IntakeFieldsTab (1587, 1631). Most of these tabs don't import or use useToast, so a save failure leaves the form frozen with no indication to the admin that anything went wrong. The Customer Config tabs (BlanketSection, APMappingSection, TemplateSection) DO use toast.show correctly — those are the template for the pattern. Impact: any transient 401/403/500 during an admin edit silently fails; admin thinks the save worked and leaves.
evidence: Admin.jsx:195 (DocumentTemplatesTab) imports no toast; catches only log to console. Compare to CustomerConfigTab children which `const toast = useToast()` and show errors via toast.
recommendedFix: Add `const toast = useToast();` at the top of every tab component that lacks one (DocumentTemplatesTab, OnboardingStepsTab, LocationTypesTab, CostCodesTab, ApplianceTypesTab, VendorsTab, IntakeFieldsTab). Replace the `catch (e) { console.error(...); }` blocks with `catch (e) { console.error(...); toast.show('err', 'Failed to save — ' + e.message); }`. Same fix in load-error handlers.

title: Admin screen has no in-component isAdmin check — relies entirely on route-level guard
detail: Admin.jsx destructures `const { user } = usePortalUser()` at line 97 but never calls isAdmin() or gates anything by role. Every tab (including Customer Config + AP Mappings which PATCH lookups, and Navigation which writes site config) is visible and editable to any user who reaches the /admin route. This works today because CR-2026-04-09-0219 added a RoleGuard wrapper on the /admin route in AppRouter.jsx (batch 01 fix). But defense-in-depth suggests the component itself should verify admin role before rendering — especially since the non-admin fallback currently relies on NavPanel hiding the /admin link and RoleGuard redirecting. If the router guard is ever removed or bypassed, every admin action is exposed.
evidence: Admin.jsx:97 `const { user } = usePortalUser();` — isAdmin/isManager are NOT destructured.
recommendedFix:
Destructure isAdmin from usePortalUser and render an access-denied fallback if isAdmin() is false: `const { user, isAdmin } = usePortalUser(); if (!isAdmin()) return
Admin access required
;`. Low priority given the route-level guard, but improves defense-in-depth.

title: CompliancePanel load + save errors swallowed to console — no toast surface
detail: Line 168 `console.error('CompliancePanel load error:', e)` — user sees nothing if rules load fails, panel just never renders. Line 202 `console.error('CompliancePanel save error:', e)` — manual checkbox toggle fails silently, user thinks click worked but the check isn't persisted. The Compliance Panel drives contract readiness scoring, so silent failures mean the score could show 'All Checks Passed' even though the save failed — false readiness indication.
evidence: CompliancePanel.jsx:167-171 load catch, 201-205 save catch — both console-only, no toast or user notification.
recommendedFix: Import useToast at the top: `import { useToast } from '../Toast';`. Inside the component, `const toast = useToast();`. In the load catch block, add `toast.show('warn', 'Failed to load compliance rules');`. In the save catch block, add `toast.show('err', 'Failed to save check — try again');`.

title: Void/Decline buttons visible to any user — comment says 'Admin only' but no role check wraps them
detail: Line 182-188 renders the Void and Decline action buttons for every non-terminal contract. The inline comment says 'Void / Decline - Admin only, non-terminal', and line 28 destructures `isAdmin, isManager` from usePortalUser — but neither variable is ever checked before rendering the buttons. Line 9 imports RoleGuard but never uses it. Any authenticated user currently sees and can click Void/Decline on any contract, triggering a forward-only, audit-logged state change. For external-customer user testing this is a real data-integrity risk: a customer clicks through the tool and nukes a live contract.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:28 `const { isAdmin, isManager, userEmail } = usePortalUser();` — isAdmin/isManager imported but unused. Line 182-188 btn-void and btn-decline rendered without a guard. Line 9 `import RoleGuard from '../RoleGuard.jsx';` — imported but never referenced elsewhere in the file.
recommendedFix: Wrap the void/decline block in `{isAdmin() && !isTerminal && (...)}` (note the `()` — isAdmin is a function per usePortalUser.jsx:112). Same pattern as CustomerDetail ProgramsTab line 506. Alternative: use the imported RoleGuard with `require="admin"`. Remove the unused RoleGuard import if not used.

title: reload() contract GET lists `dcfg_contract_number` twice in the $select clause
detail: Line 48: the $select contains `,dcfg_contract_number,...,dcfg_contract_number,...` — the column is repeated. Dataverse tolerates duplicate $select entries, so the call succeeds, but it signals the clause was edited by concatenation without review. No runtime impact, but worth cleaning up.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:48 apiGet URL — grep reveals two occurrences of dcfg_contract_number in the same comma-separated list.
recommendedFix: Delete the second `dcfg_contract_number,` from the $select list in line 48.

title: reload() error routes to top-level error banner instead of toast — replaces entire page content
detail:
Line 60: `reload().catch(e => setError(e.message)).finally(...)`. setError then causes the whole page to render `
{error}
` at line 141 — replacing the contract detail UI with a raw error string. Any transient error (network blip, 429 throttle) kills the whole screen instead of showing a dismissible toast. Also, commitTransition at line 101 uses the same pattern — a failed status-change sets the page-level error and nukes the current view.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:60 initial load, 101 commitTransition setError, 141 render `{error}` full-page.
recommendedFix: Split into two error paths: hard load failure (initial contract fetch returns null) keeps the full-page banner for clarity. Transient errors from commitTransition and later operations should use a toast (`const toast = useToast()` — already imported via Toast component elsewhere) so the user sees the failure without losing the screen.

title: Contract list load swallows errors with .catch(() => setLoading(false))
detail: Line 30: `.catch(() => setLoading(false))` — on load failure the loading spinner disappears and the table shows 'No contracts found.' which is indistinguishable from an empty state. Users cannot distinguish 'you have no contracts' from 'the load failed'. Affects external user testing because tester will report 'missing data' that's actually a 401/403/500.
evidence: ContractList.jsx:27-31 useEffect .then/.catch block.
recommendedFix:
Capture the error in state and render a distinct banner when present: add `const [error, setError] = useState(null);`, change .catch to `.catch(e => { setError(e.message); setLoading(false); })`, and render `{error &&
Unable to load contracts: {error}
}` before the table.

title: Inline searchFields array literal passed to useTableControls — defeats useMemo cache
detail: Line 21-25: `useTableControls(contracts, { ... searchFields: ['dcfg_contract_number', ...] })` — the searchFields array is allocated fresh on every render. useTableControls uses this in a useMemo dependency; a new array reference each render invalidates the memo, forcing re-filter on every keystroke/state change. Pattern is called out in Phase 1 shared-module findings as the canonical perf bug. Same issue exists in MsaList.jsx:66 and Onboarding.jsx uses a module-level constant correctly (ONBOARDING_SEARCH_FIELDS:31).
evidence: ContractList.jsx:24 — searchFields is an inline array literal.
recommendedFix: Hoist the array to a module-level constant: `const CONTRACT_SEARCH_FIELDS = ['dcfg_contract_number', 'dcfg_client_name', 'dcfg_contractor_legal_name', 'dcfg_msa_id.dcfg_customer_id.dcfg_name'];` at the top of the file, then pass `searchFields: CONTRACT_SEARCH_FIELDS` in the options object.

title: ContractList imports `isManager` from usePortalUser but never uses it
detail: Line 17: `const { isManager } = usePortalUser();` — the destructured value is never referenced in the component body. Dead import — clean up during Phase 2b console/import pass or as part of the batch fix for CR-0252.
evidence: ContractList.jsx:17. grep for isManager in this file returns only the destructure.
recommendedFix: Remove the isManager destructure — or if an admin-only action is supposed to be here, add it. Cross-check with CR-2026-04-09-0248 pattern for ContractDetail.

title: LOGO_BASE hardcoded to legacy portal URL `https://decades.powerappsportals.com/` — violates loadConfig mandate
detail: Line 25: `const LOGO_BASE = 'https://decades.powerappsportals.com/';` — this points at the LEGACY non-SPA portal, not dmms1/dcfg/holding. Per CLAUDE.md 'Config: dcfg_configs table read at boot via loadConfig() — no hardcoded URLs', every cross-environment URL should be pulled from dcfg_configs. The customer header logo src concatenates this base with LOGO_MAP[customer.dcfg_name] (line 81). On Prod today: customer avatars load from a different portal's asset library, which (a) makes Prod depend on a legacy portal being up, (b) may show stale/wrong logos if the legacy portal was updated independently, and (c) fails if the operator removes the legacy portal later in the decommission plan.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:25 `const LOGO_BASE = 'https://decades.powerappsportals.com/';`, line 81 img src=LOGO_BASE + filename.
recommendedFix: Short-term: add a `dcfg_sp_logo_base_url` key to dcfg_configs and read via `getEnvVar('dcfg_sp_logo_base_url')` with a fallback to the current hardcoded URL. Long-term: upload customer logos to a DCFG_Assets SharePoint library or the customer record itself, stop cross-portal referencing entirely. File this as infra follow-up after Phase 6.

title: CustomerDetail hardcodes `isManager={true}` / `isAdmin={true}` to sub-tabs — every user sees admin actions
detail: Lines 130, 132, 134, 135 pass hardcoded `isManager={true}` and `isAdmin={true}` to OverviewTab, MsasTab, OnboardingTab, and ProgramsTab. Line 32 destructures `isAdmin, isManager` from usePortalUser but those real values are IGNORED in favor of the hardcoded true. Downstream, those flags gate the `+ New MSA`, `+ New Onboarding Case`, `Mark Complete`, and `+ New Program` buttons — so every authenticated user sees and can click those admin-only actions. Same bug class as CR-2026-04-09-0248 (ContractDetail void/decline) but implemented by literal prop override. External customer testers will be able to create MSAs and programs.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:32 destructures isAdmin, isManager. Lines 130-135 pass `isManager={true}` / `isAdmin={true}` literally. Lines 228, 433, 443, 463, 506 in sub-components use the prop to render admin controls.
recommendedFix: Replace the hardcoded prop values with the real function calls: `isManager={isManager()}`, `isAdmin={isAdmin()}`. Same pattern as OnboardingDetail.jsx:619 which calls `isManager={isManager()}` correctly. Then smoke-test with a non-admin portal user to confirm the New MSA / New Onboarding / New Program buttons disappear from the customer detail tabs.

title: OverviewTab counts use $count=true but reads value?.length — returns top-page count, not total
detail: Lines 145-149: two apiGet calls with `$count=true` but the callback reads `msaRes?.value?.length` and `locRes?.value?.length` rather than `@odata.count`. Dataverse returns the total count as `@odata.count` when $count=true is present; `.value` is still the first page of up-to-5000 records. For customers with <5000 MSAs/locations the current code happens to work because value.length == total. For a customer with more, the KPI cards will silently show the wrong number. Low impact today but a latent data bug.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:145-149 `$count=true` with `.value.length`.
recommendedFix: Either drop `$count=true` (it's unnecessary if you're reading value.length) or read `msaRes?.['@odata.count']` to use the true total. Prefer dropping $count=true — it's not supported by Power Pages Web API consistently and value.length is fine at current scale.

title: OverviewTab nested apiGet inside .then has no error handler — unhandled promise rejection on failure
detail: Line 152-153: after the Promise.all resolves, the code makes ANOTHER apiGet inside the .then handler for contracts counts. There's no .catch on that inner promise — if it rejects, an unhandled-promise-rejection fires, caught only by the global error buffer. Line 156 also has no outer .catch on the Promise.all chain, so either root fetch failing silently skips all counts.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:144-156 — Promise.all with no outer catch, inner apiGet with no catch.
recommendedFix: Add `.catch(() => {})` or explicit error logging to both the outer Promise.all and the inner apiGet. Better: wrap the whole effect body in try/catch and set error state the user can see.

title: LocationsMapTab injects Leaflet CSS/JS from CDN at runtime — hardcoded unpkg.com URLs
detail: Lines 613, 618: `css.href = 'https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css';` and `js.src = 'https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js';`. MapView.jsx (line 10-11) imports leaflet as an npm dependency and bundles it, but CustomerDetail duplicates that functionality by injecting from CDN. Two runtime copies of Leaflet cause memory waste and potential version drift. Cat 11 handoff cleanliness.
evidence: CustomerDetail.jsx:613, 618 — CDN injection. MapView.jsx:10-11 — bundled import.
recommendedFix: Replace the CDN injection with `import L from 'leaflet'; import 'leaflet/dist/leaflet.css';` at the top of CustomerDetail (same as MapView). Remove the runtime script/link injection entirely.

title: handleSubmitForApproval calls `loadMsa()` — function is not defined in the component scope
detail: Line 83: `loadMsa();` — but there's no function named loadMsa defined anywhere in the file. The component only has the inline useEffect at line 42-58 for initial load, no named load function. Calling loadMsa() will throw ReferenceError at runtime. Result: clicking 'Submit for Approval' on an MSA succeeds in the PATCH (line 81) and the audit write (line 82), then crashes on the refresh step, leaving the UI showing the OLD status. The user thinks the submit failed and may click again, double-submitting. P1 because this is a silent data-vs-UI divergence on a money-flow action.
evidence: MsaDetail.jsx:83 `loadMsa();` — grep 'function loadMsa' or 'const loadMsa' in this file returns zero hits. The file uses an inline useEffect with no named loader, so the closure has no loadMsa symbol.
recommendedFix: Two options: (a) extract the load logic into a useCallback named loadMsa (similar to CustomerDetail.jsx:42 pattern) and call it here, OR (b) replace line 83 with a re-fetch: `const fresh = await apiGet(...); setMsa(fresh);` — same pattern as handleSaveEdit line 101. Option (a) is cleaner. Also verify by triggering the submit action in Test.

title: MsaDetail destructures `isAdmin, isManager` but never uses them
detail: Line 28: `const { user, isAdmin, isManager } = usePortalUser();` — isAdmin and isManager are destructured but the MSA edit/generate actions are rendered unconditionally (no role guard at all). Either the role checks are missing (P1 cat 9, similar to CR-0248) or these imports are dead code. Given the MSA document is the entry point to all customer billing, it is plausible that edit should be admin-only.
evidence: MsaDetail.jsx:28 destructure; no other references to isAdmin/isManager in the file.
recommendedFix: Decide per business rule: are MSA edit/generate actions restricted to admins? If YES, wrap the Edit MSA button (line 137-139) and Generate MSA button (line 143-145) in `{isAdmin() && ...}`. If NO, drop the unused destructure.

title: DocumentHistory useEffect has no error handler on the apiGet
detail: Line 243-245: `apiGet(...).then(r => setDocs(r?.value ?? []));` — no .catch, so any failure (403 on dcfg_document_outputs, 500, timeout) produces an unhandled promise rejection. The panel silently shows 'No documents generated yet.' even when the table is just unreachable.
evidence: MsaDetail.jsx:242-246 DocumentHistory useEffect.
recommendedFix: Add `.catch(() => setDocs([]))` or surface the error to a toast/banner.

title: MsaList inline searchFields array literal — defeats useTableControls useMemo cache
detail: Line 66: `searchFields: ['_customerName', 'dcfg_name']` passed inline to useTableControls. Same anti-pattern as CR-2026-04-09-0252 (ContractList) and the Phase 1 shared-module finding on useTableControls itself. Results in re-filter on every keystroke.
evidence: MsaList.jsx:63-67.
recommendedFix: Hoist to module-level constant at the top of MsaList.jsx: `const MSA_SEARCH_FIELDS = ['_customerName', 'dcfg_name'];`.

title: MsaList imports `FAMILY_MAP` and `usePortalUser` that are never referenced
detail: Line 9: `import { apiGet, FAMILY_MAP } from '../portalApi.js';` — FAMILY_MAP is never used. Line 10: `import { usePortalUser } from '../usePortalUser.jsx';` — usePortalUser is never called. Dead imports.
evidence: MsaList.jsx:9-10; grep for FAMILY_MAP and usePortalUser in this file returns only the import lines.
recommendedFix: Remove both unused imports. Part of Phase 2a dead-code sweep.

title: loadCases outer apiGet has no try/catch — loading spinner stuck on failure
detail: Lines 54-91: loadCases starts with `setLoading(true)` and directly awaits apiGet at line 64. Only the INNER progress query (line 73) has try/catch. If the outer cases query fails (401, 403, 500, network), the function throws and `setLoading(false)` at line 90 is never reached. The screen gets stuck on the skeleton banner at line 200 forever. No toast, no error banner. External testers will interpret this as 'onboarding broken' and give up.
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:54-91 loadCases function — outer fetch at line 64 has no try/catch wrapper.
recommendedFix: Wrap the entire loadCases body in try/catch/finally: `try { ...load...; } catch (err) { toast.show('err', 'Failed to load cases: ' + err.message); setCases([]); } finally { setLoading(false); }`.

title: Onboarding list destructures isManager but never uses it — +New Case visible to all users
detail: Line 44: `const { user, isManager } = usePortalUser();` — isManager destructured but not referenced. The `+ New Case` button (line 237) and the Delete/Restore buttons (lines 278-284) are rendered without any role guard. Same P2 as CR-0248/0255 but on the onboarding list. New Case creates a dcfg_onboarding_case with audit trail; Delete is soft-delete. External testers can create/delete onboarding cases.
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:44, 237, 278, 282.
recommendedFix: Wrap the New Case button in `{isManager() && ...}`. Same for the per-row Delete button. Keep Restore visible in showDeleted mode since it's a recovery action.

title: Progress query loads ALL checklist records across ALL cases (no $top, no case-id filter)
detail: Line 73-75: `apiGet('/dcfg_onboarding_checks?...$filter=dcfg_is_complete ne null')` — with no $top and no scope to the visible cases, this returns every checklist row ever created. For a system with 30 cases × 30 steps each, that's 900 rows every poll, pulled in a single query. Power Pages Web API will cap at 5000 by default but the code doesn't handle that boundary. Cat 6 performance; also a Cat 8a candidate if dcfg_onboarding_check switches to explicit-fields mode in the future.
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:72-87 progress-query block.
recommendedFix: Scope the progress query to just the cases currently in the cases list: build an `$filter=_dcfg_case_id_value in (id1,id2,...)` from the rows variable. Or switch to rolling-up dcfg_is_complete counts on the case record itself via a Power Automate flow and read them directly in the main cases query.

title: NewCasePanel declares error state that is never read or set
detail: Line 303: `const [error, setError] = useState(null);` — neither `error` nor `setError` is referenced anywhere else in NewCasePanel. Dead code.
evidence: Onboarding.jsx:303.
recommendedFix: Remove the useState declaration for error.

title: handleCreateIntakeSession uses old callFlow-style HTTP pattern instead of createDocumentRequest
detail: Lines 347-394: handleCreateIntakeSession reads `getEnvVar('dcfg_flow_intake_setup_url')` then directly `fetch(flowUrl, ...)`. This is the deprecated HTTP-trigger flow pattern. Per engineering journal §5 and CLAUDE.md, the DCFG architecture migrated to the Dataverse transaction table pattern: write to dcfg_document_requests, flow triggers on row creation. All other wizards (NewContractWizard, NewProposalWizard, CapitalPlan, ContractDetail) use createDocumentRequest(). interviewGenerate.js is cataloged in CR-2026-04-09-0006 as another stale caller. OnboardingDetail is a third stale caller.
evidence: OnboardingDetail.jsx:355-376 — getEnvVar + raw fetch against flowUrl. Compare to CapitalPlan.jsx:90-98 using createDocumentRequest.
recommendedFix: Replace the fetch block with `await createDocumentRequest({ requestType: DocRequestType.IntakeSetup, requestedBy: user?.email, name: 'Intake setup - ' + custName, customerId: custId, notes: JSON.stringify({ access_code: code, provider_name: custName, case_id: ... }) });` — may require adding IntakeSetup to the DocRequestType enum in portalApi.js. Update the flow trigger to read from dcfg_document_requests instead of HTTP. Coordinate with the intake-session flow owner.

title: handleStepFieldSave logs error to console only — no user toast
detail: Line 285-296: `handleStepFieldSave` wraps the PATCH in try/catch but only `console.error('Step field save failed:', err)`. Every other handler in this file uses toast.show('err', ...) — this one is the outlier. Admins editing a step field and hitting a save failure get no feedback.
evidence: OnboardingDetail.jsx:293 console-only catch.
recommendedFix: Add `toast?.show('err', 'Failed to save field: ' + err.message);` alongside the console.error.

title: Sensor alert location lookup interpolates raw text into GUID filter — same pattern as CR-0241
detail: Line 159: `/${EntitySets.properties}?$filter=dcfg_propertyid eq ${locId}&...` — locId comes from `rd.dcfg_location_id_text` (line 153), which could be a non-GUID value (sensor device friendly name). If non-GUID, filter generates `dcfg_propertyid eq GroupHome-12` → 400. Same pattern as SensorBanner CR-2026-04-09-0241. Also N+1: one apiGet per unique location id in the current poll, in sequence.
evidence: Operations.jsx:153-168 sensor alert location resolution loop.
recommendedFix: Same fix as CR-0241 — validate locId against GUID regex before issuing the filter. Also batch the unresolved IDs into a single `$filter=dcfg_propertyid in (...)` query instead of Promise.all individual calls.

title: fetchSensorAlerts outer `catch {}` silently swallows all errors on every 30s poll
detail: Lines 169-171: bare `catch { }` with a comment 'Sensor table may not be available — fail silently'. Fires every 30 seconds. Any post-deploy regression to dcfg_sensor_readings access or shape is invisible. Parallel to SensorBanner's CR-0242 bare catch.
evidence: Operations.jsx:169-171 bare catch in fetchSensorAlerts.
recommendedFix: Same fix as CR-0242 — add a module-level flag to log the warning once, then stay silent on subsequent polls.

title: SalesDashboard loads ALL contracts and MSAs with no $top cap and no active_flag filter
detail: Line 62: `apiGet('/dcfg_contracts?$select=dcfg_contractid,dcfg_status,...')` — no $filter for dcfg_active_flag eq true, no $top. Loads every contract ever created including soft-deleted. Line 63: same for MSAs (no filter at all). Line 64: same for customers (no filter, no $top). Dashboard is flagged as 'no caching - fresh fetch every mount' (line 4 comment JS-10), so every route change to / re-runs these. At current scale (~200 contracts) this is fine. At 2,000 contracts the dashboard becomes the single most expensive page load in the SPA.
evidence: SalesDashboard.jsx:61-68 Promise.all with 6 unbounded apiGets.
recommendedFix: Add filters where appropriate: contracts `$filter=dcfg_active_flag eq true`, MSAs `$filter=statecode eq 0`, customers `$filter=dcfg_active_flag eq true`. Add `$top=500` as a safety cap. Consider computing KPI values via a server-side Power Automate rollup stored in dcfg_configs so the dashboard reads 5 numbers instead of thousands of rows.

title: SalesDashboard imports useRef, useMemo, isManager — none are used
detail: Line 6: `import React, { useState, useEffect, useCallback, useRef, useMemo } from 'react';` — useRef, useMemo, useCallback are never used in the file. Line 41: `const { isManager } = usePortalUser();` — isManager never used.
evidence: SalesDashboard.jsx:6, 41. grep confirms no other references in this file.
recommendedFix: Trim imports to `import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';`. Remove the isManager destructure.

title: handleSendEmail uses stale callFlow('dcfg_flow_send_email_url') instead of createDocumentRequest
detail: Line 348: `await callFlow('dcfg_flow_send_email_url', { to, subject, body, reminderDays })`. Line 15 imports callFlow from portalApi — which still exists but is marked legacy per engineering journal §5 (DocGen/DMS migrated to the dcfg_document_requests transaction pattern). SendQueue is the only in-scope consumer of callFlow besides the cataloged interviewGenerate.js (CR-0006). On a Prod env where dcfg_flow_send_email_url config row isn't populated, line 348 throws — caught by the `catch {}` at line 355 which fakes success toast `'Email action logged (flow unavailable)'`. Silent misreport; user thinks the email went, nothing happens.
evidence: SendQueue.jsx:15 imports callFlow, 344-358 handleSendEmail.
recommendedFix: Replace with `await createDocumentRequest({ requestType: DocRequestType.Email, requestedBy: user?.email, name: 'Email: ' + emailModal.subject, contractId: emailModal.contractId || null, notes: JSON.stringify({ to, subject, body, reminderDays }) });`. Update the email flow to trigger on dcfg_document_requests row with requestType=Email. Replace the silent-fallback catch with an honest toast.show('err', 'Email request failed — ' + e.message).

title: SendQueue loadAll fires 5 unbounded queries at mount — contracts/msas have no $top
detail: Lines 109-114: contracts query (line 110), msas query (line 111), customers query (line 112), onboardingCases query (line 113), wipContracts query (line 114) all lack $top caps. customers filter by active only, onboarding filters by status, wipContracts filters by status+active. But contracts has only an $orderby (no filter) and msas has only $orderby+$expand. Same pattern as SalesDashboard CR-0272. The dashboard page is the SendQueue so this is the highest-traffic landing page in the SPA — every admin session hits all 5 queries.
evidence: SendQueue.jsx:109-114 Promise.all.
recommendedFix: Add `$filter=dcfg_active_flag eq true` to the contracts query. Add `$filter=statecode eq 0` to the msas query. Add `$top=500` to both as safety caps. Defer non-critical queries (onboarding, wip) until after initial render.

title: Hardcoded email addresses `team@decades-cg.com` / `compliance@decades-cg.com` in handleRequestInfo templates
detail: Line 320: `to: 'team@decades-cg.com'` — hardcoded sales team email. Line 332: email body includes `compliance@decades-cg.com` as a literal. These should come from dcfg_configs (e.g. `dcfg_email_ops_team`, `dcfg_email_compliance`) so the operator can change them without a SPA deploy.
evidence: SendQueue.jsx:320, 332.
recommendedFix: Add two dcfg_configs rows. Read via getEnvVar with fallbacks to the current hardcoded values. Update the email template to interpolate them.

title: 30s polling interval runs regardless of tab visibility — wastes cycles on background tabs
detail: Lines 61-65: `setInterval(load, 30000)` with no document.visibilityState check. Browser background tabs still run the interval (browsers throttle but don't stop). Same issue in FlowMonitor (5s interval), Operations (30s sensor, 2min WO).
evidence: AbsorptionDashboard.jsx:61-65.
recommendedFix: Wrap the load call in a visibility check: `if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') load();`. Or listen for visibilitychange and pause/resume the interval. Cat 6 performance, low priority.

title: CapitalPlan has no in-component role check — relies on AppRouter guard only
detail: CapitalPlan.jsx never calls isAdmin/isManager/hasRole. Per the post-CR-0219 routing, /capital-plan is wrapped in RoleGuard at the route level — so defense-in-depth is the only concern here. Low priority, cataloged for completeness.
evidence: CapitalPlan.jsx — grep for isAdmin/isManager returns no matches.
recommendedFix: Optional: destructure isAdmin from usePortalUser and render an access-denied fallback if false. Follows the same pattern as the Admin screen CR-0246.

title: Vendor query $select uses `dcfg_trade` but rest of SPA uses `dcfg_trades` (plural)
detail: Line 68: `&$select=...,dcfg_trade,dcfg_primary_contact` — singular `dcfg_trade`. Line 72 reads `r.dcfg_trade`. But VendorList.jsx:74 also uses `dcfg_trade` in $select, then line 138 reads `v.dcfg_trades || v.dcfg_trade` — showing the author was uncertain. MsaList.jsx:62, portalApi.js fetchVendors (if it exists) and other places reference `dcfg_trades`. Only one of the two names is correct. If `dcfg_trades` is the actual schema (comma-separated list per ProjectList.jsx:25 TRADES list), then Directory shows '' for every vendor (field not returned, fallback to empty string).
evidence: Directory.jsx:68, 72. VendorList.jsx:74, 138. Inconsistent usage across files.
recommendedFix: Verify via Dataverse EntityDefinition which column actually exists on dcfg_vendor. Update Directory.jsx to match — most likely `dcfg_trades` is the correct name. Cross-check with the Database Bible (`reference_database_bible.json`).

title: Directory imports usePortalUser but never uses it
detail: Line 9: `import { usePortalUser } from '../usePortalUser.jsx';` — never called anywhere in the file.
evidence: Directory.jsx:9.
recommendedFix: Remove the unused import.

title: FlowMonitor polls every 5 seconds with no pause-on-hidden check
detail: Line 74: `setInterval(fetchRequests, POLL_INTERVAL)` where POLL_INTERVAL=5000. Every 5 seconds fetches up to 50 document request rows + expansion on template. Internal admin tool, low-traffic, but if left open in a background tab for an hour that's 720 unnecessary hits to Dataverse. Same class as CR-0277 (AbsorptionDashboard).
evidence: FlowMonitor.jsx:7 POLL_INTERVAL=5000, 74 setInterval.
recommendedFix: Gate on `document.visibilityState === 'visible'` before fetching. Or listen for visibilitychange events to stop/resume the interval.

title: MapView caps properties query at $top=2000 — silent truncation above that
detail: Line 63: `$top=2000` — hardcoded cap. Current scale is ~150 locations so not an issue. But if a customer onboards with 2500 sites, the map silently drops the last 500. No UI indication. Latent data-completeness risk.
evidence: MapView.jsx:63.
recommendedFix: Keep the cap but add a warning banner when the result is exactly 2000: `if (locs.length === 2000) toast.show('warn', 'Map showing first 2000 locations — filter by customer to see the rest');`.

title: NoraCopilot hardcodes Copilot Studio webchat URL with environment GUID
detail: Line 10: `var WEBCHAT_URL = 'https://copilotstudio.microsoft.com/environments/6ee0cd74-e2b2-e429-ac4b-27123cd20d19/bots/cua_agent_iRkq7/webchat?__version__=2';` — the environment GUID `6ee0cd74-...` is baked into the SPA bundle, so Test and Prod render the SAME Nora bot. If a different Copilot Studio env is used per stage, every deploy has to rebuild the bundle. Violates the loadConfig mandate in CLAUDE.md.
evidence: NoraCopilot.jsx:10.
recommendedFix: Move the webchat URL to dcfg_configs as `dcfg_nora_webchat_url`. Read via `getEnvVar('dcfg_nora_webchat_url')` with the current value as fallback. Allows per-env override without a SPA build.

title: ProgramDetail loadProgram silently swallows load errors with .catch(() => setLoading(false))
detail:
Line 46: `.catch(() => setLoading(false))` — no error state, no toast. On failure, loading spinner turns off and the page shows `

Program not found.

` at line 86, which is indistinguishable from a real 404. Same anti-pattern as ContractList CR-0251.
evidence: ProgramDetail.jsx:46.
recommendedFix: Add `const [error, setError] = useState(null);` and distinguish load failure from not-found. Show a toast or error banner on load failure.

title: Save as Template uses browser prompt() — bad UX for external testing
detail: Line 239: `const tplName = prompt('Template name:', `${project.dcfg_name} Template`);` — native browser prompt is blocking and visually inconsistent with the rest of the SPA's SlideOutPanel/modal UI. External customer testers will see a system dialog that breaks the navy/amber brand.
evidence: ProjectDetail.jsx:239.
recommendedFix: Replace with an inline modal or SlideOutPanel for template-name entry. Match the SlideOutPanel usage pattern from NewRfpWizard or Admin.jsx forms.

title: Template-line copy loop is sequential N+1 — 20-line template = 20 sequential POSTs
detail: Lines 183-197: for-loop with `await apiPostReturnId(...)` inside creates one HTTP round-trip per line. At typical template sizes (~10-30 lines) this delays project creation by 2-5 seconds. Same pattern as NewContractWizard line 527 (contract lines) and TemplateDetail line 658 (template fields).
evidence: ProjectList.jsx:183-197.
recommendedFix: Use `Promise.all` to parallelize: `await Promise.all(tplLines.map(line => apiPostReturnId(...)))`. Preserves the intended behavior with a ~10x speedup on networks with any latency.

title: New Project panel load-customers/templates/properties apiGets have no error handlers
detail: Lines 83-88: three useEffect apiGet calls when the new-project panel opens. None has a .catch — silent failure results in empty dropdowns with no explanation. Cat 3.
evidence: ProjectList.jsx:83-88.
recommendedFix: Add `.catch(() => {})` at minimum or preferably surface a toast warning on first failure.

title: ProjectList destructures isManager but never uses it
detail: Line 55: `const { isManager } = usePortalUser();` — never referenced. Same pattern as several other screens in this wave.
evidence: ProjectList.jsx:55.
recommendedFix: Remove the unused destructure. Or add role-gating to the `+ New Project` button if intended.

title: toggleCheck calls `toast(...)` as a function, but toast is an object — TypeError on every checklist toggle
detail: Line 140: `toast(`Updated: ${key.replace('dcfg_','').replace(/_/g,' ')}`, 'ok');`. Line 142: `toast(e.message, 'err');`. But line 45 sets `const toast = useToast();` which returns an OBJECT with a `.show()` method (verified against other files like ContractDetail.jsx:77, SendQueue.jsx:77, OnboardingDetail.jsx:92 — all use `toast.show('ok', ...)`). Calling `toast(...)` directly throws 'TypeError: toast is not a function'. Result: EVERY click on an RFP procurement checklist item crashes the handler, the checkbox state does not persist (except the optimistic setRfp at line 139 which runs BEFORE the toast call so actually the state IS updated — but the user sees a crash in the console, and the audit log entry never gets written). P0 because this is a production bug on a core RFP workflow screen.
evidence: RfpDetail.jsx:140, 142 — `toast(...)` calls. Line 45 `const toast = useToast();`. Toast.jsx exports useToast returning `{ show: (level, msg) => ... }` per other consumers.
recommendedFix: Change line 140 to `toast.show('ok', 'Updated: ' + ...);` and line 142 to `toast.show('err', e.message);`. Match the pattern used elsewhere in the file — except THERE IS NO `toast.show` call anywhere in this file, all uses of `toast` are wrong. Fix both call sites.

title: Procurement checklist references `dcfg_contract_fe` — field name mismatch with portalApi.js $select
detail: Line 131: `{ key: 'dcfg_contract_fe', label: 'Contract Fully Executed' }`. But portalApi.js line 772 RFP_LIST_COLS selects `dcfg_contract_fee` (as fixed in Phase 1 batch 01 per CR-2026-04-09-0209). There is a mismatch: the $select returns `dcfg_contract_fee` (money column), but the checklist key is `dcfg_contract_fe` (doesn't exist). When user toggles this checklist item, updateRfpPackage is called with `{ dcfg_contract_fe: true }` → Dataverse 400 (unknown field). Compounded with the toast-as-function bug CR-0289, the user sees nothing happen. The correct column name is almost certainly `dcfg_contract_fully_executed` (to match the label) OR `dcfg_contract_fee_exec` (speculation). NEEDS SCHEMA VERIFICATION before fix.
evidence: RfpDetail.jsx:131, RfpList.jsx:63 both reference `dcfg_contract_fe`. portalApi.js:772 RFP_LIST_COLS contains `dcfg_contract_fee` (the money column, not a boolean flag).
recommendedFix: Query Dataverse EntityDefinition for dcfg_rfp_package boolean columns: `EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='dcfg_rfp_package')/Attributes?$filter=AttributeType eq 'Boolean'&$select=LogicalName`. Identify the 'fully executed' boolean, likely `dcfg_contract_fully_executed`. Update RfpDetail.jsx:131, RfpList.jsx:63, and portalApi.js RFP_LIST_COLS to use the correct name. If the column does not exist, add it via solution then update consumers.

title: RfpList checklist progress reads `r.dcfg_contract_fe` — always undefined, progress stuck at 3/4 max
detail: Line 63: `const checkCount = [r.dcfg_bid_solicited, r.dcfg_bid_received, r.dcfg_scope_exhibit_drafted, r.dcfg_contract_fe].filter(Boolean).length;`. `dcfg_contract_fe` does not match the portalApi.js $select (which requests `dcfg_contract_fee`) nor any known boolean column. The server returns `dcfg_contract_fee` (money), the code reads `dcfg_contract_fe` (undefined), filter(Boolean) drops it, checkCount never reaches 4. Every RFP package displays at most 3/4 progress regardless of actual state.
evidence: RfpList.jsx:63. portalApi.js:772 RFP_LIST_COLS.
recommendedFix: Same fix as CR-2026-04-09-0290 — verify schema and update the key everywhere (RfpList.jsx:63, RfpDetail.jsx:131, portalApi.js:772).

title: UserRolesTab queries `/mspp_webroles` and `/contacts` directly — may 400 per engineering journal Sec 11
detail: Per engineering journal Section 11, the Power Pages Web API (`/_api/`) only supports custom data tables (`dcfg_*`). System tables like `mspp_*`, `contacts`, `environmentvariabledefinitions` are documented as inaccessible. UserRolesTab.jsx makes FOUR such calls: line 119 `/mspp_webroles`, line 131 `/contacts`, line 147 `/mspp_webroles(id)?$expand=mspp_webrole_contact`, line 190 `apiDelete('/contacts(id)/mspp_webrole_contact(roleId)/$ref')`, line 195 POST to `mspp_webrole_contact/$ref`, line 250 `/contacts?$filter=emailaddress1`, line 258 apiPostReturnId '/contacts'. The engineering journal §20 notes the N:N nav property `mspp_entitypermission_webrole` returns 0 records even when links exist — platform limitation. If the same is true for `mspp_webrole_contact`, this entire tab cannot work via Web API. The operator's documented workaround is Power Pages admin center UI for role assignments. NEEDS VERIFICATION against the actual Prod portal — if the calls DO work (perhaps because DCFG enabled the tables in a site setting), the finding downgrades to P3 informational. If they don't, this tab is dead code and should be marked as such or rebuilt.
evidence: UserRolesTab.jsx:119, 131, 147, 190, 195, 250, 258. reference_engineering_journal.md Section 11 'Portal Web API Cannot Access System Tables'. Section 2 'Web Role Assignment in Enhanced Data Model' — notes 4+ attempts failed.
recommendedFix: Three-step: (1) operator loads the Admin → User Roles tab on Prod and checks the network tab — confirms whether /_api/mspp_webroles and /_api/contacts 400 or return data. (2) If they 400, mark the tab as a known-broken feature in the Admin UI with a 'Use Power Pages admin center' link. (3) Eventually replace with a custom dcfg_user_role_assignment table the SPA can read/write directly, or a Power Automate flow that proxies the mspp_ operations via application-auth.

title: VendorDetail $select requests `dcfg_contact_name` and `dcfg_trade` — likely incorrect schema names
detail: Line 16: `$select=dcfg_vendorid,dcfg_legal_name,dcfg_display_name,dcfg_contact_name,dcfg_phone,dcfg_email,dcfg_address,dcfg_trade,dcfg_active_flag`. Two suspect columns: (1) `dcfg_contact_name` — Admin.jsx VendorsTab $select at line 1134 uses `dcfg_primary_contact` not `dcfg_contact_name`. (2) `dcfg_trade` — same singular-vs-plural conflict as CR-0279. Both may cause the $select to return partial data or (worse) fail entirely if Dataverse rejects unknown columns.
evidence: VendorDetail.jsx:16; Admin.jsx:1134 — the only other `dcfg_vendors` $select in scope — uses `dcfg_primary_contact`.
recommendedFix: Verify vendor column schema via Dataverse EntityDefinition. Update VendorDetail $select to match actual columns. Also align with the fetchVendors helper in portalApi.js if present.

title: VendorList $select omits dcfg_latitude/dcfg_longitude but distance-search reads them — geo filter always empty
detail: Line 74: `$select=dcfg_vendorid,dcfg_display_name,dcfg_legal_name,dcfg_address,dcfg_city,dcfg_state,dcfg_email,dcfg_phone,dcfg_trade,dcfg_active_flag`. No dcfg_latitude, no dcfg_longitude. But line 115 reads `v.dcfg_latitude` and `v.dcfg_longitude` to compute haversine distances. Those fields are undefined on every row, so distance search always returns zero matches. The 'Distance Search' feature in the Vendor List is visually present but never works against database vendors.
evidence: VendorList.jsx:74 $select, 115 distance computation.
recommendedFix: Add `dcfg_latitude,dcfg_longitude` to the $select on line 74. Confirm dcfg_vendor has these columns (not all vendors will — the distance-search UI may need geocoding on first use).

title: VendorList geocodes via hardcoded `nominatim.openstreetmap.org` URL
detail: Line 83: `fetch('https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?format=json&q=' + ...)` — hardcoded third-party geocoding service. OpenStreetMap's Nominatim has a usage policy limiting to 1 req/sec and requiring a User-Agent header. This fetch sets neither, so heavy use could get the SPA IP-banned from the free Nominatim instance. Should be configurable via dcfg_configs and should set a User-Agent.
evidence: VendorList.jsx:79-102 doDistanceSearch.
recommendedFix: Move the geocoder URL to dcfg_configs (`dcfg_geocoder_url`). Add a User-Agent header identifying the DCFG portal. Consider caching geocoded addresses in localStorage to avoid re-geocoding the same search.

title: Field registry maps 'Contract value' to `dcfg_contract_value` — column does not exist (journal Sec 9)
detail: Line 109: `{ label: 'Contract value', path: 'dcfg_contract_value', category: FieldCategory.WorkOrderTerms, isComposite: false }`. Per engineering journal Section 9 Schema Quick Reference: `dcfg_contract_value` — does not exist anywhere. On dcfg_contract the correct column is `dcfg_contract_fee`. Every template that maps a highlight to 'Contract value' produces a Dataverse path that resolves to undefined at document-generation time. The DocGen V4 flow reads the dcfg_template_field rows and looks up each path on the source record — undefined → blank in the generated document. Same issue line 525 in TemplateDetail.jsx composite definition for contract_value_written which also references `dcfg_contract_value`. P0 because this breaks document generation for every template using 'Contract value' mapping.
evidence: fieldRegistry.js:109. TemplateDetail.jsx:525-527 composite. Engineering journal Section 9 'Columns that don't exist'.
recommendedFix: Change path on line 109 from `dcfg_contract_value` to `dcfg_contract_fee`. Keep the label 'Contract value' for user familiarity. Same fix for TemplateDetail.jsx line 525 and 526 composite parts. Verify by opening an existing template with this mapping and confirming `dcfg_dataverse_path` now resolves on the dcfg_contract record.

title: Field registry maps 'Amendment number' to `dcfg_amendment_no` — journal Sec 9 says use `dcfg_amendment_sequence`
detail: Line 59: `{ label: 'Amendment number', path: 'dcfg_amendment_no', category: FieldCategory.ContractIdentifier, isComposite: false }`. Per engineering journal Section 9: `dcfg_amendment_number` — use `dcfg_amendment_sequence`. The registry uses `dcfg_amendment_no` which matches neither the wrong name nor the right name. Compare to NewContractWizard.jsx:336 which correctly writes `payload.dcfg_amendment_sequence = parseInt(...)`. Templates mapping 'Amendment number' will produce blanks in every generated amendment document.
evidence: fieldRegistry.js:59. NewContractWizard.jsx:336 (correct name).
recommendedFix: Change the path on line 59 from `dcfg_amendment_no` to `dcfg_amendment_sequence`.

title: Amendment financials paths are speculative — need schema verification before declaring fixed
detail: Lines 116-120: paths `dcfg_original_amount`, `dcfg_prev_changes_amount`, `dcfg_current_amount`, `dcfg_change_amount`, `dcfg_approved_amount`. None of these are referenced anywhere else in the SPA (grep returns zero matches in other files). Either the amendment flow is not yet live (so no one noticed the paths are broken) or the paths are wrong. Per engineering journal Section 9, `dcfg_contract_value` on dcfg_contract does not exist. These five amendment columns are adjacent semantically and likely share the same suspect provenance.
evidence: fieldRegistry.js:116-120. Grep across /src for any of these five paths returns only this file.
recommendedFix: Verify each path against the actual dcfg_contract schema. Likely correct names follow the pattern `dcfg_*_fee` or `dcfg_*_amount` — run `EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='dcfg_contract')/Attributes?$filter=contains(LogicalName,'amount') or contains(LogicalName,'amendment')&$select=LogicalName`. Update fieldRegistry accordingly. Until verified, any template using these mappings will emit blanks.

title: Vendor composite references `dcfg_vendor.address1_city_state_zip` — not a standard Dataverse column
detail: Lines 65-73 and 74-75: paths `dcfg_vendor.address1_line1` and `dcfg_vendor.address1_city_state_zip`. The `address1_line1` pattern is standard Dataverse composite-address field naming (same as contact/account). But `address1_city_state_zip` is NOT a standard composite — Dataverse composites are typically `address1_composite` (full block) or separate `address1_city`, `address1_stateorprovince`, `address1_postalcode`. The path as written will resolve to undefined. Templates mapping 'Vendor city, state, zip' produce blanks.
evidence: fieldRegistry.js:65-75. Dataverse standard address fields are address1_line1, address1_line2, address1_city, address1_stateorprovince, address1_postalcode, address1_composite.
recommendedFix: Either: (a) change the path to `dcfg_vendor.address1_composite` and accept the full address block format, (b) concatenate `address1_city + ', ' + address1_stateorprovince + ' ' + address1_postalcode` in the DocGen flow (server-side), or (c) add a calculated field `dcfg_vendor_city_state_zip` to the vendor table.

title: handleSave template-fields loop is sequential N+1 — large templates take N × round-trip
detail: Lines 658-680: `for (var i = 0; i < localFields.length; i++) { await apiPostReturnId/apiPatch(...) }`. One HTTP round-trip per field. A template with 40 fields = 40 sequential POST/PATCHes. At ~200ms per round-trip on Power Pages that's 8 seconds of blocking UI for a save. Worse, lines 683-692 then do ANOTHER sequential loop for audit log writes. Combined: 2N sequential calls.
evidence: TemplateDetail.jsx:658-680 field save loop, 683-692 audit loop.
recommendedFix: Parallelize both loops with Promise.all. Risk: race condition on writeAuditLog ordering — acceptable since order is preserved in dcfg_performed_at. Field save loop: `await Promise.all(localFields.map(async (f, i) => { const body = ...; if (f.dcfg_template_fieldid) await apiPatch(...); else { body['dcfg_template_id@odata.bind'] = ...; await apiPostReturnId(...); } }));`. Same treatment for audit log loop.

title: Composite `contract_value_written` references non-existent `dcfg_contract_value` and `dcfg_contract_value_written`
detail: Lines 522-528: `contract_value_written` composite defines parts with paths `dcfg_contract_value_written` and `dcfg_contract_value`. Per engineering journal Section 9, `dcfg_contract_value` does not exist; it should be `dcfg_contract_fee`. `dcfg_contract_value_written` similarly likely doesn't exist (no grep hits across /src). Same bug as CR-0296 but in the getCompositeParts function used by the detection code path — auto-detected composites pick the wrong paths.
evidence: TemplateDetail.jsx:522-528.
recommendedFix: Change line 526 path to `dcfg_contract_fee`. For line 525, either create `dcfg_contract_fee_written` calculated field in Dataverse or remove the written form from the composite (use only the numeric).

title: doToggle uses raw picklist ints `100000007`/`100000008` instead of AuditActionType enum names
detail: Line 150: `actionType: newActive ? 100000007 : 100000008, // Template Activated / Deactivated`. The magic numbers are AuditActionType.Created (100000007) and AuditActionType.Deleted (100000008) per portalApi.js:96, but the labels 'Template Activated/Deactivated' don't match Created/Deleted. Either the enum is wrong (then we need new values) or the usage is wrong (should reuse StatusChanged = 100000006). Cat 11 handoff cleanliness.
evidence: TemplateList.jsx:150. portalApi.js:96 AuditActionType map.
recommendedFix: Replace with `actionType: AuditActionType.StatusChanged` — template activation is a status change, not a create/delete. Drop the raw ints. If business needs distinct audit types for activation, add `TemplateActivated`/`TemplateDeactivated` values to AuditActionType with new picklist values.

title: saveAllFields has two sequential N+1 loops — save and audit, both serial
detail: Lines 87-91 saveField loop: `for (const f of fieldList) { await saveField(f); ... }`. Lines 100-110 writeAuditLog loop: `for (const f of fieldList) { if (f.dcfg_dataverse_path) { await writeAuditLog(...); } }`. Same problem as TemplateDetail.jsx CR-0300 — the hook is where the N+1 ultimately lives. Callers (TemplateDetail) may not know this.
evidence: useTemplateFields.js:87-110.
recommendedFix: Parallelize both loops with Promise.all. Same pattern as CR-0300. Audit log writes are fire-and-forget so Promise.all is safe.

title: useContractData loads ALL contracts client-side then paginates in memory
detail: Line 31: `fetchContractsPaginated('')` — the 'Paginated' name is misleading; it fetches all contracts in one query (Power Pages does not support $skip so server-side pagination is not an option). Client-side slice at line 72. Works today at ~200 contracts. Scales poorly to 2,000+.
evidence: useContractData.jsx:29-41.
recommendedFix: Accept the current pattern — Power Pages limitation is real. Add `$top=5000` cap to fetchContractsPaginated as a safety. Document the scale ceiling in a comment. Mitigation path: switch to a server-side rollup table when load exceeds 1000 contracts.

title: handleGenerate contract-lines create loop is sequential — 10-line exhibit = 10 round-trips
detail: Lines 527-538: `for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) { ...; await createContractLine(...); }`. Each line is one sequential POST. Typical contracts have 5-15 lines; each adds ~200ms; total ~2-3s of blocking on the generate click. saveLinesToDataverse (line 381) has the parallel version of the same logic. Inconsistent with itself.
evidence: NewContractWizard.jsx:527-538. Compare to saveLinesToDataverse:389 which uses Promise.all.
recommendedFix: Parallelize with Promise.all — same pattern as saveLinesToDataverse. Risk: Dataverse rate-limiting at very high concurrency, acceptable at typical line counts.

title: Stray `)}` JSX closer at line 942 — same as pre-seed CR-2026-04-09-0001
detail: Confirmed presence of the orphan `)}` at line 942 with the 'Vendor is selected on Step 3' comment at line 941. This is the exact block called out in pre-seed CR-2026-04-09-0001. Documented here so the expansion audit's file-by-file coverage doesn't miss it. Cross-referenced, no duplicate fix needed.
evidence: NewContractWizard.jsx:941-942 exactly match the pre-seed finding.
recommendedFix: Covered by CR-2026-04-09-0001 — delete lines 941-942.

title: generate() picks 'first active vendor' as Decades vendor — fragile defaulting
detail: Line 384: `const vr = await apiGet(`/${EntitySets.vendors}?$filter=dcfg_active_flag eq true&$select=dcfg_vendorid&$top=1`); vendorId = vr.value?.[0]?.dcfg_vendorid`. Picks whichever active vendor happens to be first in the default sort order. On a fresh tenant with multiple active vendors, the 'first one' could be Acme HVAC instead of Decades Construction Group. The subsequent patch (lines 385-390) then writes the Decades signer info to the wrong vendor record, corrupting its data. The 'Decades vendor' should be identified by a canonical flag or ID pulled from dcfg_configs.
evidence: NewProposalWizard.jsx:384-390.
recommendedFix: Add a dcfg_configs entry `dcfg_decades_vendor_id` (the GUID of the canonical Decades vendor). Read via getEnvVar and use as the hardcoded-but-configurable vendor id. Fallback to the current 'first active vendor' only if the config is missing.

title: MSA-rates create loops are sequential — one POST per location type
detail: Lines 440-467: both the uniform branch (lines 440-452) and the type-based branch (lines 453-467) use sequential for-loops with await inside. With 6-8 location types, that's 6-8 sequential POSTs per proposal generation. Parallelizing cuts wall-clock generation time by ~4-5 seconds.
evidence: NewProposalWizard.jsx:440-467.
recommendedFix: Promise.all both loops. Same pattern as CR-0305, CR-0300. Minor risk of Dataverse rate-limiting at 8 concurrent POSTs, acceptable.

title: ContractsList.jsx remains as dead-code duplicate of screens/ContractList.jsx — see pre-seed CR-0003
detail: Confirmed during file-by-file walk: src/ContractsList.jsx is a 'three switchable views' wrapper that imports from contracts/* but is not referenced by the live router. The active contract-list screen per AppRouter is src/screens/ContractList.jsx (a separate shorter file). Pre-seed CR-2026-04-09-0003 already captures this; this finding is here only to document the expansion audit touched the file and agrees with the pre-seed verdict. No separate audit needed — skip detailed findings.
evidence: ContractsList.jsx header comment 'Three switchable production views'. screens/ContractList.jsx is the live router target.
recommendedFix: Covered by CR-2026-04-09-0003 — operator approves deletion.

title: Admin VendorsTab $select includes `dcfg_trade` — same singular vs plural uncertainty as Directory/VendorList
detail: Line 1134: `$select=...` — but actually no, line 1134 lists the known columns and the `dcfg_trade` is NOT in it. Actually re-reading: `dcfg_vendorid,dcfg_legal_name,dcfg_display_name,dcfg_address,dcfg_city,dcfg_state,dcfg_zip,dcfg_phone,dcfg_email,dcfg_primary_contact,dcfg_signer_name,dcfg_signer_title,dcfg_payment_terms,dcfg_payment_process,dcfg_active_flag`. No trade column in the Admin list.
